p.src: Now Cao Rui, Emperor of Wei, appointed Zhang He as vanguard and ordered him to advance with Sima Yi; at the same time, he ordered Xin Pi and Sun Li to lead fifty thousand troops to Cao Zhen's aid. The two departed in obedience to the edict.

u.src: Now Cao Rui, Emperor of Wei, appointed Zhang He as vanguard and ordered him to advance with Sima Yi;
at the same time, he ordered Xin Pi and Sun Li to lead fifty thousand troops to Cao Zhen's aid.
The two departed in obedience to the edict.

p.src: Meanwhile, Sima Yi led two hundred thousand troops through the pass and made camp. Summoning the vanguard commander Zhang He to his tent, he said, “Zhuge Liang has always been cautious and has never dared act rashly. Were I commanding his army, I would long ago have marched straight through Ziwu Valley and seized Chang'an. It is not that he lacks strategy; he merely fears a reverse and refuses to take risks. He will now surely bring his army through Xie Valley to seize Mei. If he moves against Mei, he must divide his forces into two routes, sending one army to take Ji Valley. I have already issued orders for Zidan to hold Mei and not to give battle when the enemy comes; and for Sun Li and Xin Pi to block the mouth of Ji Valley and strike with a surprise force when the enemy arrives.” Zhang He asked, “Where, then, will you advance, General?” Sima Yi replied, “I have long known that west of the Qinling Mountains lies a road through a place called Jieting, beside which stands a city named Lieliu; both places are vital throats of Hanzhong. Zhuge Liang believes Zidan unprepared and will certainly advance by this route. You and I shall march straight for Jieting; from there Yangping Pass is not far. When Zhuge Liang learns that I have cut the vital road at Jieting and severed his supply line, he will be unable to hold the Longxi region securely and must flee back to Hanzhong by night. If he retreats, I shall lead troops along the byways and strike him, winning a complete victory; if he does not return, I shall fortify and block every byway and post troops to guard them all. After a month without provisions, all the Shu troops will starve, and Zhuge Liang must fall into my hands.” Suddenly comprehending, Zhang He bowed to the ground and said, “Your calculations are divine, Commander!” Sima Yi said, “Even so, Zhuge Liang is no Meng Da. As vanguard, General, you must not advance rashly. Pass word to every commander to follow the road west of the mountains and scout far ahead. Only when there are no ambushers may you advance. If you grow careless, you will surely fall into Zhuge Liang's trap.” Zhang He received the plan and led his army away.

p.src: Meanwhile, as Kongming sat in his camp at Mount Qi, word suddenly came that a scout from Xincheng had arrived. Kongming hurriedly summoned him and questioned him. The scout reported, “Sima Yi marched at double speed and reached Xincheng in only eight days, catching Meng Da wholly unprepared; moreover, Shen Dan, Shen Yi, Li Fu, and Deng Xian aided the enemy from within, and Meng Da was slain amid the fighting. Sima Yi has now withdrawn to Chang'an, met the Emperor of Wei, and come through the pass with Zhang He at the head of an army to oppose us.” Kongming was greatly startled. “Meng Da acted without secrecy, so his death was inevitable. Now that Sima Yi has passed through the barrier, he will surely seize Jieting and cut the road that is our very throat.” He then asked, “Who dares lead troops to defend Jieting?” Before he had finished, Staff Officer Ma Su said, “I am willing to go.” Kongming said, “Though Jieting is small, its importance is immense: if Jieting is lost, our entire army is finished. Although you are deeply versed in strategy, the place has neither walls nor natural barriers and is exceedingly difficult to defend.” Ma Su replied, “I have studied the military classics since childhood and know the art of war reasonably well. Could I possibly be unable to defend a mere Jieting?” Kongming said, “Sima Yi is no ordinary opponent; and his vanguard Zhang He is a renowned general of Wei. I fear you cannot withstand him.” Ma Su said, “Never mind Sima Yi and Zhang He—even if Cao Rui came in person, what would there be to fear? If anything goes amiss, I beg you to execute my entire family.” Kongming said, “There are no idle words in the army.” Ma Su replied, “I am willing to sign a military pledge.” Kongming consented. Ma Su then wrote out the military pledge and presented it.

p.src: Kongming said, “I shall give you twenty-five thousand picked troops and assign another able general to assist you.” He summoned Wang Ping and instructed him, “I have always known you to be cautious, and therefore specially entrust this grave duty to you. You must act with the utmost care. Make camp at the strategic road there, so that the enemy cannot slip through at short notice. Once the camp is established, draw a map showing the terrain in every direction and send it for my inspection. Settle every matter through consultation before acting, and do nothing lightly. If you keep the position secure, yours will be the foremost merit in the taking of Chang'an. Be warned! Be warned!” The two took their leave and led the troops away. Reflecting that the two might meet with disaster, Kongming summoned Gao Xiang and said, “Northeast of Jieting stands a city called Lieliu, reached by a remote mountain road; troops may be stationed and encamped there. I give you ten thousand troops; go and garrison that city. If Jieting is endangered, lead your troops to its rescue.” Gao Xiang led his troops away. Kongming then reflected that Gao Xiang was no match for Zhang He: an able general must be stationed to the right of Jieting before it could be secure. He therefore summoned Wei Yan and ordered him to lead his own troops and encamp behind Jieting. Wei Yan said, “As commander of the van, I ought by rights to be first to break the enemy. Why place me in an idle position?” Kongming replied, “Breaking the enemy as vanguard is merely the work of a subordinate commander. I now order you to support Jieting, guard the vital road leading to Yangping Pass, and defend the very throat of Hanzhong: this is a grave responsibility. How can you call it idle? Do not regard it lightly and ruin my great enterprise. You must exercise the utmost care!” Wei Yan was delighted and led his troops away. Only then did Kongming feel at ease. He summoned Zhao Yun and Deng Zhi and instructed them, “Sima Yi's present deployment differs from those of former days. Each of you is to lead an army through Ji Valley as a diversion. If you encounter Wei troops, whether you engage them or not, keep them in alarm. I shall personally command the main army through Xie Valley and march straight upon Mei. If Mei falls, Chang'an can be taken.” The two received their orders and departed. Kongming appointed Jiang Wei as vanguard and sent the army through Xie Valley.

p.src: Now Ma Su and Wang Ping led their troops to Jieting and surveyed the terrain. Ma Su laughed and said, “Why is the Prime Minister so needlessly anxious? In such a remote mountain district as this, how would the Wei army dare come?” Wang Ping said, “Though the Wei army may not dare come, we should encamp below at this junction of five roads; then order the soldiers to fell timber and build a stockade, as a measure for holding out.” Ma Su said, “How could the middle of a road be a place to pitch camp? Beside us stands a mountain, unconnected on all four sides and thickly wooded. This is a natural stronghold bestowed by Heaven. We can station the army atop it.” Wang Ping said, “You are mistaken, Army Adviser. If we station our troops across the road and build defensive walls, even a hundred thousand enemy soldiers could not slip past us; but if we abandon this vital road and camp upon the mountain, what plan could save us should the Wei army suddenly arrive and surround us on every side?” Ma Su laughed loudly. “Yours is truly a woman’s judgment! The art of war says, ‘Looking down from commanding heights, one’s force is like a blade splitting bamboo.’ If the Wei army comes, I shall see that not one man returns in armor!” Wang Ping said, “I have followed the Prime Minister through many battles, and wherever we went, he instructed me in every detail. In my view, this mountain is untenable ground. If the Wei army cuts off our route to the water, our soldiers will fall into disorder without even fighting.” Ma Su said, “Do not talk nonsense! Sun Tzu says, ‘Cast them onto deadly ground, and only then will they live.’ If the Wei army cuts off our route to the water, will the soldiers of Shu not fight to the death? Then each man will be a match for a hundred. I have long studied military texts, and even the Prime Minister consults me on many affairs. How dare you obstruct me?” Wang Ping said, “If you insist on encamping upon the mountain, then divide off some troops for me. I shall establish a small camp west of the mountain, so that the two positions may support each other. Should the Wei army arrive, we can answer each other’s needs.” Ma Su would not agree. Suddenly, inhabitants of the mountain came racing toward them in groups, reporting that the Wei army had arrived. Wang Ping wished to take his leave. Ma Su said, “Since you refuse to obey my command, take five thousand troops and go establish your own camp. But when I have defeated the Wei army, do not expect to share the credit before the Prime Minister!” Wang Ping led his troops ten li from the mountain and made camp. He drew a map and that very night dispatched a man to report to Kongming, explaining in full that Ma Su had encamped upon the mountain.

p.src: Meanwhile, Sima Yi, while in the city, ordered his second son, Sima Zhao, to scout the road ahead; if troops were guarding Jieting, the army was to hold its position and advance no farther. Sima Zhao obeyed, scouted the area, then returned and told his father, “Troops are guarding Jieting.” Sima Yi sighed. “Zhuge Liang is truly a man of divine ability. I am no match for him!” Sima Zhao laughed. “Father, why do you discourage yourself so? I believe Jieting can easily be taken.” Sima Yi asked, “How dare you make so bold a claim?” Sima Zhao replied, “I reconnoitered it with my own eyes. There is neither camp nor stockade upon the road, and all the troops are stationed on the mountain. That is how I know they can be defeated.” Sima Yi was delighted. “If the troops truly are on the mountain, Heaven itself means me to succeed!” He changed his clothes and personally rode out with over a hundred horsemen to inspect the place. That night the sky was clear and the moon bright. He went straight to the foot of the mountain, reconnoitered all around it, and only then returned. Seeing him from the mountain, Ma Su laughed loudly. “If he values his life, he will not come to surround this mountain.” He passed an order to his commanders: “If the enemy comes, watch for the red flag waving on the summit, then charge down from all four sides.”

p.src: When Sima Yi returned to camp, he sent men to learn which commander was leading the troops guarding Jieting. They reported back, “It is Ma Su, the younger brother of Ma Liang.” Sima Yi laughed. “He has nothing but an empty reputation. He is merely mediocre! How could Kongming employ such a man and not bring disaster upon his cause?” He asked again, “Are there any other troops to either side of Jieting?” A scout reported, “Wang Ping has made camp ten li from the mountain.” Sima Yi ordered Zhang He to lead a force and block Wang Ping’s route of approach. He also ordered Shen Dan and Shen Yi to lead two forces around the mountain and first cut off the routes to the water; once the Shu troops fell into disorder, they were to seize the advantage and attack. All deployments were settled that night. At daybreak the next morning, Zhang He led his troops around to the rear first. Sima Yi drove his great army forward in a mass and completely surrounded the mountain. Looking down from the mountain, Ma Su saw Wei soldiers covering hill and plain, their banners and ranks in perfect order. At the sight, the Shu troops all lost heart and dared not descend the mountain. Ma Su waved the red flag, but officers and men pushed one another forward, and not a single man dared move. Enraged, Ma Su personally killed two commanders. Terrified, the soldiers had no choice but to muster their strength, descend the mountain, and charge the Wei army. The Wei troops stood perfectly still. The Shu troops retreated up the mountain again. Seeing that matters had gone awry, Ma Su ordered the troops to guard the camp gates closely and wait for aid from outside.

p.src: Meanwhile, when Wang Ping saw the Wei army arrive, he led his troops into the attack and encountered Zhang He; after more than a score of bouts, his strength was spent and his position isolated, so he had no choice but to retreat. The Wei army kept the mountain under siege from the hour of the dragon until the hour of the dog. With no water on the mountain, the soldiers could not prepare food, and the camp fell into great disorder. The clamor continued until midnight, when the Shu troops on the southern side threw open the camp gates, descended the mountain, and surrendered to Wei. Ma Su could not restrain them. Sima Yi then ordered men to set fires all along the mountain, throwing the Shu troops above into still greater confusion. Realizing that he could not hold the position, Ma Su drove his surviving troops down the mountain and fled westward. Sima Yi opened a broad avenue and allowed Ma Su to pass. Zhang He then led his troops in pursuit from behind. After they had pursued for more than thirty li, drums and horns sounded together ahead. A strong force emerged, let Ma Su pass, and blocked Zhang He; it was Wei Yan, who brandished his blade, spurred his horse, and charged straight at Zhang He. Zhang He turned his force and fled. Wei Yan drove his troops in pursuit, intending to retake Jieting. After he had pursued for more than fifty li, a great cry arose and ambush troops poured out from both sides: Sima Yi on the left and Sima Zhao on the right swept behind Wei Yan and trapped him in the center of their encirclement. Zhang He returned, and the three forces joined together. Wei Yan charged left and broke right but could not escape, and more than half his troops were lost. At the height of the danger, a strong force suddenly charged into the fray. It was Wang Ping. Wei Yan cried joyfully, “I shall live!” The two commanders joined their forces and fought a fierce engagement, whereupon the Wei troops finally withdrew. But when the two commanders hurried back to camp, they found it filled with the banners of Wei. Shen Dan and Shen Yi charged out from the camp. Wang Ping and Wei Yan made straight for Lieliu and sought refuge with Gao Xiang.

p.src: At this time, Gao Xiang learned that Jieting had been lost. He mustered all the troops of Lieliu and went to the rescue, meeting Wei Yan and Wang Ping on the way, who told him what had happened. Gao Xiang said, “We had better raid the Wei camp tonight and retake Jieting.” The three men settled their plan below the hillside. As dusk approached, they divided their forces into three columns. Wei Yan led the advance and went straight to Jieting. Seeing no one there, he grew deeply suspicious and dared not advance rashly, so he lay in ambush at the road entrance and waited. Presently Gao Xiang’s troops arrived, and the two commanders discussed how they had no idea where the Wei forces were. While they were still at a loss, Wang Ping’s troops also failed to appear. Suddenly a cannon boomed; flames leapt to the sky and drums shook the earth. The Wei troops poured out together and surrounded Wei Yan and Gao Xiang on every side. The two fought with all their strength to break through, but could not escape. Suddenly, from behind the hillside came battle cries like thunder. A body of troops charged in—it was Wang Ping, who rescued Gao Xiang and Wei Yan, and they fled straight toward Lieliu. By the time they reached the city walls, another force had already arrived beside the city. Its banner bore in great characters: “Guo Huai, Commander of Wei.” It turned out that Guo Huai and Cao Zhen had conferred, fearing that Sima Yi would claim all the merit, and so Guo Huai had been detached to take Jieting. When he learned that Sima Yi and Zhang He had already accomplished the feat, he led his troops in a direct surprise attack on Lieliu. He encountered the three commanders, and a fierce battle followed. The Shu troops suffered very heavy casualties. Fearing that Yangping Pass might also be lost, Wei Yan hurried there with Wang Ping and Gao Xiang.

It turned out that Guo Huai and Cao Zhen had conferred, fearing that Sima Yi would claim all the merit, and so Guo Huai had been detached to take Jieting.
When he learned that Sima Yi and Zhang He had already accomplished the feat, he led his troops in a direct surprise attack on Lieliu.
He encountered the three commanders, and a fierce battle followed.
The Shu troops suffered very heavy casualties.
Fearing that Yangping Pass might also be lost, Wei Yan hurried there with Wang Ping and Gao Xiang.

p.src: Now Guo Huai gathered his troops and said to those around him, “Though I failed to take Jieting, I have captured Lieliu, which is also a great achievement.” He led his troops straight to the city walls and called for the gates to be opened. At once a cannon sounded from the ramparts and banners rose everywhere. The foremost great standard read: “Sima Yi, Commander Who Pacifies the West.” Sima Yi raised the hanging drawboard, leaned against the protective wooden railing, and laughed. “Why are you so late, Boji?” Guo Huai exclaimed in astonishment, “Zhongda, your divine foresight is beyond me!” He then entered the city. After they had exchanged greetings, Sima Yi said, “Now that Jieting has been lost, Zhuge Liang is certain to retreat. You must quickly join Zidan and pursue him through the night.” Guo Huai followed his advice and departed from the city. Sima Yi summoned Zhang He and said, “Zidan and Boji came to take this city because they feared I would win all the merit. Yet I have no wish to claim success alone; what I have achieved was merely a stroke of fortune. I expect that Wei Yan, Wang Ping, Ma Su, Gao Xiang, and the rest will first go to occupy Yangping Pass. If I go to seize that pass, Zhuge Liang will surely attack me from behind, and I shall fall into his trap. The art of war says, ‘Do not press an army returning home; do not pursue a desperate foe.’ Take a bypath and move to intercept the retreating troops from Jigu Valley. I shall personally lead troops to meet those from Xie Valley. If they flee in defeat, do not bar their way. Simply intercept them midway, and all the Shu army’s baggage and supplies will fall into our hands.” Zhang He accepted the plan and departed with half the troops. Sima Yi then gave the order: “Advance directly upon Xie Valley, proceeding by way of Xicheng. Though Xicheng is a small, remote mountain county, it is where the Shu army stores its provisions and also the junction of the main roads to the three commanderies of Nan’an, Tianshui, and Anding. If we take that city, the three commanderies can be recovered.” Thereupon Sima Yi left Shen Dan and Shen Yi to guard Lieliu, while he personally led the main army toward Xie Valley.

p.src: Now after Kongming had sent Ma Su and the others to defend Jieting, he remained uneasy and uncertain. Suddenly a messenger from Wang Ping arrived with a map. Kongming ordered him admitted, and his attendants presented the map. Kongming opened it on his writing table and examined it. Striking the table in alarm, he cried, “Ma Su is a fool! He has doomed my army!” Those around him asked, “Why is the Prime Minister so alarmed?” Kongming replied, “From this map I see that he has abandoned the vital road and pitched camp upon the mountain. If the Wei army arrives in force, surrounds him on every side, and cuts off the path to the water, his troops will fall into disorder by themselves within two days. If Jieting is lost, where can we retreat?” Chief Clerk Yang Yi stepped forward and said, “Though I possess little talent, I am willing to replace Ma Youchang.” Kongming carefully instructed Yang Yi in every detail of how to establish the camp. Just as Yang Yi was about to depart, a mounted courier suddenly arrived and reported that both Jieting and Lieliu had been lost. Kongming stamped his foot and sighed deeply. “The great enterprise is lost! This is my fault!” He urgently summoned Guan Xing and Zhang Bao and instructed them: “Each of you is to lead three thousand elite troops and take the bypath toward Mount Wugong. If you encounter Wei troops, do not engage them in force. Merely beat the drums and raise a great clamor, frightening them with a feigned army. They will withdraw of their own accord, but you must not pursue them. Once all our troops have withdrawn, make your way to Yangping Pass.” He also ordered Zhang Yi to lead troops ahead and repair the defenses at Jiange, securing the route of retreat. He then secretly issued orders for the main army to quietly pack its baggage and prepare to depart. He ordered Ma Dai and Jiang Wei to cover the rear, first concealing themselves in a mountain valley and withdrawing only after all the other troops had retreated. He also sent trusted men by separate routes to order the officials, soldiers, and people of Tianshui, Nan’an, and Anding to move into Hanzhong. He sent another trusted man to Ji County to escort Jiang Wei’s aged mother into Hanzhong.

p.src: Once Kongming had completed these arrangements, he first led five thousand troops to Xicheng County to transport the provisions. Suddenly more than ten mounted couriers arrived in rapid succession, reporting that Sima Yi was leading an army of one hundred and fifty thousand in a massed advance upon Xicheng. At that time Kongming had no great commanders beside him, only a group of civil officials. Of the five thousand troops he had brought, half had already gone ahead to carry provisions, leaving only two thousand five hundred soldiers within the city. When the officials heard this news, they all turned pale. Kongming climbed the city wall and looked out. Sure enough, dust billowed to the heavens as the Wei forces advanced upon Xicheng County in two columns. Kongming issued orders that all banners and standards be hidden. The officers were each to guard their assigned posts upon the walls, and anyone who moved in or out without authorization or spoke loudly was to be executed at once. He had all four gates thrown wide open and stationed twenty soldiers at each, disguised as commoners and sweeping the streets. If the Wei army arrived, no one was to move without orders, for he had a plan of his own. Kongming then donned a crane-feather cloak and a silk scholar’s cap. Taking two young attendants to carry a zither, he seated himself by the railing before the tower above the gate, lit incense, and began to play.

p.src: Now Sima Yi’s scouts reached the foot of the city walls. Seeing this strange scene, none dared advance, and they hurried back to report to Sima Yi. He laughed and would not believe them, so he halted the whole army and rode forward alone to observe from afar. Sure enough, he saw Kongming seated atop the gate tower, smiling serenely as he burned incense and played the zither. To his left stood a boy holding a precious sword; to his right, another boy held a yak-tail whisk. Inside and outside the city gate, more than twenty townspeople swept the ground with lowered heads, oblivious to all around them. After watching, Yi grew deeply suspicious. He returned to the center of his army, ordered the rear guard to become the vanguard and the vanguard the rear guard, and withdrew toward the road north of the mountains. His second son, Sima Zhao, said, “Could it not be that Zhuge Liang has no troops and is merely putting on this display? Why, Father, do you withdraw at once?” Yi replied, “Liang has always been cautious and has never taken reckless risks. Now that he has thrown the city gates wide open, there must be an ambush. If our troops advance, we shall fall into his trap. What would you young men know of it? We must retreat at once.” Thus the troops on both routes withdrew completely. When Kongming saw the Wei army receding into the distance, he clapped his hands and laughed. The assembled officers were all astounded. They asked Kongming, “Sima Yi is a renowned general of Wei. Today he came here commanding a hundred and fifty thousand elite troops, yet the moment he saw the Chancellor, he swiftly withdrew. Why was that?” Kongming replied, “He judged that I have always been cautious and would never take a reckless risk. Seeing such a scene, he suspected an ambush and therefore withdrew. I do not make a habit of courting danger; I used this stratagem only because I had no other choice. He will surely lead his army away by the narrow road north of the mountains. I have already ordered Guan Xing and Zhang Bao to wait for him there.” All were amazed and said admiringly, “The Chancellor’s subtle designs are beyond the fathoming even of spirits and gods. Had it been left to men like us, we would surely have abandoned the city and fled.” Kongming said, “I had only two thousand five hundred soldiers. At a sudden cannon blast from behind the mountain, Shu troops swept toward them over every hill and field; the generals at their head were Jiang Wei and Ma Dai. Cao Zhen was terrified. Just as he hurriedly ordered a retreat, his vanguard commander Chen Zao was slain by Ma Dai. Cao Zhen led his army back in a panic, while the Shu troops all hurried through the night to Hanzhong.

p.src: Meanwhile, Guo Huai led his troops back into the road through Jigu Valley. Just as he was about to overtake the Shu troops, a red banner with white lettering emerged from behind the hillside, bearing the name “Zhao Yun.” Su Yong hastily drew back his troops and fled. Before he had gone several li, a tremendous cry arose and a body of troops burst forth; at their head rode a great general, spear leveled as his horse leapt forward, shouting, “Do you know Zhao Zilong?” Su Yong exclaimed in terror, “How can Zhao Yun be here as well?” Caught wholly unprepared, he was thrust from his horse and killed by a single stroke of Zhao Yun’s spear, and the rest of his troops scattered. Yun continued slowly forward. Another force then approached from behind, commanded by Guo Huai’s subordinate Wan Zheng. Seeing the Wei troops pursuing hard, Yun reined in his horse, leveled his spear, and took his stand at the road entrance to await the approaching general in combat. By then the Shu troops had gone more than thirty li. Wan Zheng recognized Zhao Yun and dared not advance. Yun waited until dusk before turning his horse and withdrawing at an unhurried pace. When Guo Huai’s troops arrived, Wan Zheng told him that Zhao Yun was as valiant as ever and that he had therefore dared not approach. Huai ordered the army to pursue at once, and Zheng sent several hundred stout cavalrymen racing after him. When they reached a great forest, they suddenly heard a mighty shout behind them: “Zhao Zilong is here!” More than a hundred Wei soldiers were so frightened that they fell from their horses, while all the rest fled over the ridge. Wan Zheng forced himself to engage, but Yun shot an arrow into the tassel of his helmet, startling him so badly that he tumbled into a ravine. Pointing his spear at him, Yun said, “I shall spare your life and let you go back! Quickly tell Guo Huai to come after me!” Wan Zheng escaped with his life and returned. Yun escorted the wagons, equipment, troops, and horses toward Hanzhong without losing a single thing along the way. Cao Zhen and Guo Huai retook the three commanderies and claimed the achievement as their own.
